construct: Claudin-16 is a tight-junction protein in the thick ascending limb that participates with claudin-19 in paracellular reabsorption of magnesium and calcium. CLDN16 loss causes renal magnesium wasting, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive kidney disease.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and biallelic CLDN16 loss identifies FHHNC from defective claudin-16-dependent paracellular divalent-cation reabsorption in the thick ascending limb.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: TRPM6 mediates distal convoluted-tubule transcellular magnesium entry, while NCC, NKCC2, and proximal Na/K-ATPase represent different transport proteins or nephron segments; none is the CLDN16 tight-junction lesion.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The genotype plus the paired magnesium/calcium wasting phenotype directly determine the paracellular TAL mechanism.
